body:
The native outbox write-path review for #1916 confirmed that the shared MutationOutboxStorage port does not declare `discardSupersededNoteRecovery`, so the native adapter cannot provide the web shared-notes cleanup behavior through that port.

Follow up on the shared-notes migration: measure the web adapter and callers, define the required recovery-discard operation in the shared port when that consumer is lifted, and run one behavioral contract against web and native adapters. Preserve unrelated recovery records and define what counts as superseded before implementing it.

This is the pre-existing follow-up recorded in the D25d handoff, outside the current native write/read adapter split (#1916/#1917). Related conformance suite: #1927. No backward-compatibility layer is requested.

Independent audit of #1917 at73fff461 confirms that the existing web settleReceipt and settleApplied implementations already remove older notes/human/set recovery rows for the same target and lower sequence. Native omits that semantic side effect; a separate public method is not necessary to express it. No current native producer or approved D25d-1 through D25d-4 piece submits notes/human/set (those pieces cover send, steer, queue, interrupt, rendering and discovery).

This issue is a required prerequisite before any native notes producer lands: document the shared settlement contract, add the native sweep within both existing settlement transactions, and exercise the same contract for both adapters. Tests must preserve unrelated methods/targets/newer rows and prove rollback if the sweep fails. Do not treat structural interface conformance alone as proof of this semantic parity.
